Uncle Munir was the neighbourhood baker. He baked every morning at dawn, and people bought their hot bread from him.

Tamim passed his bakery every morning on his way to school, and Uncle Munir would give him a little ka'k biscuit and say, "Here — to give you strength for your lessons."

Uncle Munir had borrowed money from Tamim's father, Hajj Rashid, to fix his oven when it broke down, and he had promised to pay it back at the end of the year.

When the end of the year came, he came to Hajj Rashid with his head bowed.

He said, "Hajj, business was slow this year, and my wife fell ill. I only have half the money. Please give me more time."

Hajj Rashid said, "The money is mine, and I've already given you a whole year." There was anger in his voice.

Uncle Munir left, sad. Tamim had heard everything.

The next morning he passed by the bakery and found Uncle Munir baking alone, his face tired — and he did not give him a ka'k.

When Tamim came back from school, he said to his father, "Baba, Uncle Munir has given me a ka'k every day for years, and he's never once taken money for it."

Then he said, "Shouldn't we give him back what he gave us?"

Hajj Rashid was quiet. Then he took out the mushaf and recited: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ ۚ وَأَن تَصَدَّقُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾

And he said, "It means: if the person in debt is poor, give him time until he is able to pay. And if you let him off his debt, that is better for you."

Then he said, "And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter.'"

Tamim said, "So will Allah make things easy for us if we make things easy for him?" His father said, "That is Allah's promise."

In the morning Hajj Rashid and Tamim went to the bakery. When Uncle Munir saw them, he was afraid and said, "Hajj, I haven't collected the rest yet."

Hajj Rashid said, "I've come to tell you: the half you gave me — take it for your wife's medicine. And as for the rest, I've let it go."

Uncle Munir cried and made a long du'a for them.

Then he took a big, hot ka'k out of the oven, split it between Tamim and his father, and said, "This one isn't for sale."

That year, business in Hajj Rashid's shop grew so much that he was amazed. And Tamim would say, "That's Allah's promise, Baba."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter."

📖 Narrated by Muslim. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
